paper.claim: One total durable-evidence classifier prioritizes Commit, conclusive Fail, Unknown after non-conclusive Failure, Retry, and residual Unknown; the stored durable query is exactly equal to replay, and the lost-reply witness preserves distinct zero- and one-effect worlds.

premises: classification uses only replayed durable phase, typed attempt outcomes, retry class, and the configured attempt bound
the Journal prefix is legal when the classifier is consumed by a record guard
the K4 lost-reply witness uses one Uncontrolled Authorize/Prepare/Arm/Start(1) prefix
conclusions: durable Success prevents retry and selects Commit
conclusive Failure selects Fail, while a latest non-conclusive Failure selects Unknown before retry eligibility
the durable-state implementation of the classifier equals replay exactly
the same lost-reply prefix classifies Unknown and both the zero-effect and one-effect worlds satisfy k4_a3_unknown_effect_cardinality_allowed while remaining distinct

caveats: Evidence-complete means complete relative to the durable record language, retry class, and attempt budget; it does not reveal an unpersisted remote linearization or claim epistemic maximality over arbitrary external systems.

paper.claim: Successful-result soundness, resolved-failure soundness, and effect boundedness form a reusable primitive adapter interface whose generic composition derives AdapterVerified; the Idempotent, ReadOnly, and Deduplicated packages instantiate that interface.

premises: a compatible Commit must satisfy result_spec and the class-appropriate zero-effect or one-effect relation
a compatible resolved Fail must satisfy zero_effect
every external run admitted by AdapterRely must satisfy zero_effect or one_effect
conclusions: the three primitive laws imply the retained AdapterVerified terminal-refinement interface
the EnsureMember, ReadOnly, and Deduplicated packages derive AdapterVerified through the same generic lemma

caveats: The primitive laws make adapter assumptions explicit but do not verify arbitrary production adapters, remote services, or deployment isolation.

paper.claim: Every admitted recovery episode extends committed history monotonically, and every recovery Commit cites a matching successful Outcome already durable at the crash prefix.

premises: wal_runtime_layer::exec(cfg, execution)
t5_r0_layer::recovery_episode(execution.events, crash, finish)
recovery repair is enabled only while mode != Mode::Online
a recovery Commit must match request, attempt, value, and outcome_ref in the crash-prefix durable Journal
conclusions: is_prefix(alpha_commit_wal(crash), alpha_commit_wal(finish + 1))
wal_recovery_episode_has_crash_prefix_provenance(execution, crash, finish)
Commit, Fail, Unknown, and NotRecovery are classified exhaustively

caveats: The theorem is about the typed WAL model and does not refine byte persistence or the Rust broker.

paper.claim: For any well-formed adapter whose primitive laws derive AdapterVerified, storage context, and plugged WAL execution satisfying the adapter rely relation, the canonical Broker terminal and per-request effect refinement are transported from the WAL execution; complete mediation transports when the coupled projection premise is supplied.

premises: the PaperConfig is well formed and its adapter satisfies the primitive laws that generically derive AdapterVerified
storage_parametric_context and plugged_wal_exec relate the context and typed WAL
adapter_rely holds for the selected request and external run
the WAL has the stated terminal outcome; the P0 prefix product supplies any protected-call coupling needed for mediation
conclusions: the canonical Broker has the same terminal outcome and adapter projection
the terminal refines the adapter abstract run and satisfies per_request_effect_refinement
complete mediation is transported from the coupled projection rather than assumed by the generic terminal theorem

caveats: This is a conditional composition theorem: it does not construct a coverage member or prove arbitrary adapters, services, Rust executions, or byte persistence.
The generic terminal theorem and the separate mediation transport lemma must not be read as an unconditional protected-effect guarantee.

paper.claim: For a request-indexed Deduplicated family that covers every terminal request, each selected family member supplies the generic contextual composition obligations and yields a mediated, adapter-relative terminal refinement.

premises: every terminal request is covered by a DD5OperationalMember whose stable key and coupled adapter/protected executions match the WAL
the member derives the DD4 prefix product, adapter rely, and protected-call mediation obligations
the generic T6-X0 contextual premises hold for the shared typed WAL and storage context
conclusions: the family statement holds for every terminal request and its selected member
canonical Broker terminal/effect refinement and complete mediation are obtained per request
the DD2 family witness proves non-vacuity of the request-indexed coverage endpoint

caveats: The family theorem is coverage-conditioned; production Rust does not automatically construct or discharge DD5 family members.
The retained non-vacuity witness is the Deduplicated DD2 instance, not a proof that every deployment satisfies the family premises.

paper.claim: The executable typed-record kernel checks preview, post-WAL commit, crash/recovery control, durable-success Commit, terminal evidence, and class-sensitive resume for its supported record alphabet.

premises: the input is a structurally legal sequence under a well-formed immutable manifest
kernel commit occurs only after the caller supplies the durable WAL LSN
resume is permitted only by the class-sensitive recovery predicate
conclusions: typed durable state and LSN/cut coupling are preserved
durable-success recovery Commit is accepted without another adapter invocation
unsafe Uncontrolled/ReadOnly prefixes remain fail closed

caveats: Revoke, byte encoding, filesystem durability, and whole-program Rust control flow remain outside this target.

paper.claim: Selected real Rust broker append/replay traces pass through the compiled K4 gate at exact durable cuts and exercise terminal and recovery branches.

premises: the harness supplies a proof-erased K4-A4 library and a manifest-bound broker configuration
the selected append path previews before WAL and commits after the durable LSN
reopen replays the complete durable prefix before serving requests
conclusions: the exercised traces conform at typed-record prefixes, cuts, terminal state, and recovery classification

caveats: This is finite integration evidence, not a whole-program Rust or byte-WAL refinement theorem.

paper.claim: The retained submission evaluation uses immutable manifests and a K4 gate for every broker open, and attests preview/commit pairing, replay, and recovery closure.

premises: every submission configuration carries an immutable admission manifest
the evaluation has no ungated Broker::open fallback
the retained attestation is validated independently

caveats: The attestation checks the retained evaluation configuration; it does not prove arbitrary Rust executions or deployment isolation.

symbols: this is not an implementation-refinement theorem
